entities.title: Every typed operation calls the JSON layer
entities.summary: The typed layer has no date, zone or text logic of its own: each operation writes UTV JSON, calls the 0.2 function and converts its result.
entities.context: Library 0.3 adds a typed layer on top of the 0.2 JSON layer, whose behaviour the shared everyday and text-form fixtures pin down.
entities.decision: CivilDate.AddMonths calls Calendar.Add, ZonedIntent.Resolve calls Zones.Resolve, Interval<T>.Contains calls Ranges.Contains, ToString calls TextForm.Format, and so on. Typed.Total turns a result into a plain value; Typed.ToOutcome into an Outcome<T>.
entities.rationale: docs/library-api.md §2: every operation must agree with the JSON-level everyday API, and so with the fixtures, and implementations should call the 0.2 functions underneath rather than re-implement them.

entities.title: Temporal.Parse and period.Components
entities.summary: Where the shared naming collides with C#, the C# library uses Temporal.Parse for the contract's Utv.Parse, and reads period components as period.Components.Days.
entities.context: docs/library-api.md §6 names the general parser Utv.Parse and gives Period both static builders (Period.Days(30)) and component properties.
entities.decision: Temporal.Parse(text) and Temporal.FromJson(json) return Outcome<ITemporalValue>; Period exposes its components as a PeriodComponents record struct in Components.
entities.rationale: Utv is the namespace in C#, so Utv.Parse cannot be a method; a static Period.Days(30) and an instance Days cannot share a name. library-api §6 records both deviations.

entities.title: Outcome<T> as an abstract record with nested cases
entities.summary: The five outcome cases are sealed records nested in Outcome<T>, so a pattern reads Outcome<CivilDate>.None(var why) anywhere.
entities.context: docs/library-api.md §3 asks each language for its own exhaustive sum type. C# has no closed unions.
entities.decision: abstract record Outcome<T> with a private protected constructor, and nested sealed records Unique, Multiple, None, Unsupported and Invalid, each with a Deconstruct. Callers shorten names with a using alias per result type (using DateOutcome = Utv.Outcome<Utv.CivilDate>) or using static.
entities.rationale: The README: the case names are nested, so they work anywhere. The cost, also stated in the README, is that C# does not know the five cases are all there are, so a switch expression needs a final _ => arm.

entities.title: Years are BigInteger
entities.summary: CivilDate and CivilYearMonth hold the year as System.Numerics.BigInteger, and Of takes one.
entities.context: UTV years are decimal strings of any length; docs/library-api.md §1 asks for arbitrary-precision years (BigInteger in C# and Java).
entities.decision: Year is a BigInteger in the typed values, in GregorianCivil and in the internal day arithmetic (CivilMath), with astronomical numbering (year 0 exists).
entities.rationale: Arbitrary precision: no year is out of range for the library, only for .NET's own types, which then say so (out-of-native-range).
